change.description: Consolidate target verification feature transfers after all transformer layers. Reuse the existing verification-logit workspace until the output projection runs. Arithmetic, projections, weights, samplers, controller and scalar decoding are unchanged.
change.workspace: Ensure capacity before captures using max(batch_size, ceil(batch_size * captured_layer_count * hidden_size / vocab_size)). Qwen27B feature width is 5*5120=25600, below vocabulary width248320, so this uses the existing allocation. No new persistent buffer, kernel or execution option.
change.ordering: Five D2D tap captures; contiguous D2H feature transfer and last-row D2D transfer; output projection overwrites the workspace, all on arena_.stream. The final-hidden/no-tap branch is preserved.
change.maintained_test: Extend the existing target_test scalar/verification comparisons to check all five DFlash2 taps (layers6,20,34,48,62) and the retained final row. No new test executable, model load or sweep.

release.method: Q4 target/Q4 draft, C1, greedy. Adaptive raw JSON/prose TG300: two timed samples per binary in ABBA order, 32-token raw JSON warmup per binary excluded. Fixed-7 repetition chat TG128: two paired samples per binary in ABBA order. Includes prefill, excludes model loading. All IDs checked against preceding qualified AR references; scalar code unchanged.

quality.postprocessing: Validated completed qualification logs; no model tests repeated.

profile.method: Separate release C1 raw JSON TG300 runs with rocprofv3 --hip-trace --kernel-trace --memory-copy-trace. All 300 IDs match qualified AR; 285 drafted, 256 accepted and 43 rounds in both runs. These traced runtimes are not release throughput measurements.
profile.source_transfer_change: Per verification round, five strided D2H tap copies and five last-row D2D copies become five strided D2D captures, one contiguous D2H copy and one last-row D2D copy. Total explicit transfer API calls fall from 10 to 7. All copies precede logits reuse on the same stream.
profile.interpretation: The layer-loop hipMemcpy2DAsync API wait disappears; waiting on earlier GPU work shifts to the final contiguous hipMemcpyAsync and later kernel submissions. API duration is not pure transfer cost and is not additive to kernel time. The speed claim comes only from the unprofiled ABBA runs.
profile.copy_trace_limit: The memory-copy trace does not enumerate every API transfer directly: the runtime also implements copies with internal kernels. Before/after kernel counts differ only for those copy implementations. Do not interpret the baseline absence of MEMORY_COPY_DEVICE_TO_HOST events as absence of host transfers.

generation_roi.boundary: First exact K-quant projection start to last Gufo kernel end; excludes initialization and prefill, and a few initial draft kernels. API counts include only calls fully inside this interval. Traced timings are attribution controls, not release throughput.

rejected_q6_expansion.scope: Actual Q6_K vocabulary head, two full-mantissa seeds, all outputs finite/bit-exact. Original mapping, byte-identical anonymous copy and same-code clone controls; ten balanced rounds with six launches per variant. Original/clone instruction hashes match, all variants have zero scratch. No model qualification needed for a rejected isolated layout.

limits: Two timed samples per binary/workload, not a significance study or full depth/concurrency sweep.
The 102 full-vocabulary and 102 tapped-feature rows compare verification with scalar execution on both target quants; they do not independently qualify the original target checkpoint or MTP.
The 46 named sampling cases validate bounded seeded replay and deterministic parity. Sampled AR and DFlash2 continuations may differ because they consume different RNG sequences.
Draft arithmetic is untouched and its target features are exact. The all-three-draft upstream trace comparison and full target/draft/controller/HTTP matrix were not repeated for this transfer change.
The Q6 expansion test changes storage only and was rejected for speed. No changed-numerics route was adopted.
No 75-question capability comparison was run. Full depth refresh, independent original-checkpoint/MTP qualification and complete C>1 speculative qualification remain open.
Laurent FP4 headline uses different artifacts/settings and decode-only timing; these including-prefill measurements do not establish that goal was reached.

normalization_cost_controls.decision: No production change. The two-barrier reduction is deferred because its isolated benefit projects below 0.1% of total inference time. The single-wave variant is rejected for a large slowdown. No additional full-model build, sweep, maintained test or tool.
normalization_cost_controls.operator_contract: Keep each original thread subtotal and the 128,64,32,16,8,4,2,1 addition tree. Two-barrier variant reads paired LDS subtotals in the first wave, then uses wave shuffles. Single-wave variant holds the original eight per-lane partial sums in registers and uses the same tree, with no LDS.
normalization_cost_controls.quality: Each harness checks two full-mantissa seeds, weighted and unweighted normalization, FP32 and BF16 outputs, dimensions 1,31,32,63,127,128,255,256,257,511,512,4096,5120,10240,25600 and batches 1,3,4,7,8,16,128. Every output is finite and bit-identical to production, including clone controls. The combined graph harness checks 94,646,916 output elements per dtype. This is operator parity, not an independent checkpoint qualification.
normalization_cost_controls.method: Balanced variant ordering; nine rounds for three variants, eight rounds for four variants. Graph replay checks whether CPU launch overhead masks the norm timing. Correctness precedes timing. No power/clock changes.
normalization_cost_controls.finding: At verification widths 3,4,7,8, the two-barrier variant saves about 0.30us per call, about 4.6% more norm throughput, in direct and graph controls. Norm is about 1.4% of the release profile, so extrapolation would be roughly 0.06% total throughput if the isolated ratio carried over. This is an estimate, not an end-to-end gain. The batch 128 result varies between harnesses. The single-wave variant takes about 5.6 times as long at small widths despite zero spills.
